scope: Independent exact original-control replay of twofailed and onepassing Lift originals; onlyinitial reset and recorded robotctrlwrites. Contactforces sampled immediatelyaftermj_step, geometrytime labels explicit; no source/object/model/gate changes.
interpretation: Lift4 closure27.03mm tracking error coincides with240.19N forearm/table load and the independently inspected nominal path has15.665mm table penetration; this is fixture obstruction, not evidence that a free-space servo is intrinsically too slow.

Lift5 first bilateral acquisition has1.70mm TCP error. It later drifts4.83deg primarily about boxZ while TCP error is0.091mm; measured jaw skew reduces10.87deg to6.05deg. Its source-relative reference rotation is much smaller.
Passing Lift6 has23.3mm TCP lag at the lift anchor but only0.93deg box-face skew and1.18deg eventual rotational drift; peak tracking error alone does not explain success.

The four rotation-only failures do not share identical axes: axis alignment is most directly motivated for Lift5/15. Lift16/23 already have smaller face skew and stronger other-axis rotation; the same bounded intervention is diagnostic there, not guaranteed recovery.
